meal.title: Adding Comments in C
meal.objective: Add single‑line and multi‑line comments and the const keyword to C code

voice.script: What if your code could talk without saying a word? How do you add notes to C code? In C you can write remarks that the compiler ignores. A double slash starts a single‑line comment that runs to the end of that line. Anything after the slashes is just a note for humans. For longer explanations you open with slash‑asterisk and close with asterisk‑slash; everything in between is ignored, even across many lines. You can also mark a value as constant with the const keyword, which tells the compiler the variable never changes, and you often add a comment explaining why. Here’s a tiny program. // This prints a greeting /* The next line declares a constant integer */ const int answer = 42; printf("The answer is %d\n", answer); When you run it, the only output is the greeting line with the number, because all the comments vanished during compilation. Remember: comments are your way to document code without affecting what runs. Try adding a comment above each line of a program you write today.
